security_spec.violation_condition: Kernel code that detects Smidctrl/Ssidctrl and then reads eidelivery to infer ACLIC delivery mode, or writes to eithreshold for interrupt threshold control instead of using mithreshold. The old spec guaranteed eidelivery=0x20000000 when Smidctrl/Ssidctrl present, but the new spec removes eidelivery/eithreshold from Smidctrl/Ssidctrl scope entirely, making their values implementation-defined and their semantics unrelated to ACLIC operation.
security_spec.summary: eidelivery/eithreshold removed from Smidctrl/Ssidctrl scope: kernel must not assume eidelivery indicates ACLIC mode nor write eithreshold for ACLIC thresholds—use mithreshold instead

findings.finding: KVM IMSIC VS-file local_read saves/restores eidelivery and eithreshold via CSR_VSISELECT/CSR_VSIREG indirect access. This is pure IMSIC virtualization under the AIA spec's VS-file model, not Smidctrl/Ssidctrl. No riscv_isa_extension_available(SMIDCTRL) check exists; the code is gated by KVM AIA init which checks SSAIA only.

spec_citations.excerpt: The AIA eidelivery and eithreshold CSRs defined for the Incoming Message Signaled Interrupt Controller (IMSIC) are not included in the scope of Smidctrl/Ssidctrl.

findings.finding: imsic_local_delivery() writes IMSIC_EITHRESHOLD and IMSIC_EIDELIVERY via indirect CSR access (SISELECT/SIREG). This is the IMSIC driver's local-delivery enable/disable path, called from CPU hotplug online and PM resume. It is gated by riscv_isa_extension_available(NULL, SxAIA) at init time, not by SMIDCTRL/SSIDCTRL. This code operates on IMSIC hardware, not ACLIC domains.

spec_citations.excerpt: The AIA eidelivery and eithreshold CSRs defined for the Incoming Message Signaled Interrupt Controller (IMSIC) are not included in the scope of Smidctrl/Ssidctrl.

findings.finding: imsic_setup_state() uses riscv_isa_extension_available(NULL, SxAIA) to gate IMSIC probing. If a platform implements ACLIC (Smidctrl/Ssidctrl) and firmware advertises Smaia/Ssaia for the ACLIC hart-level AIA dependency, this check would match, causing the IMSIC driver to probe and attempt to read/write IMSIC_EIDELIVERY/IMSIC_EITHRESHOLD via indirect CSRs. On a pure ACLIC system without IMSIC hardware, those registers are not in the Smidctrl/Ssidctrl scope (per spec line 340), so their values would be implementation-defined. This is a config-time risk: the kernel cannot distinguish IMSIC-capable AIA from ACLIC-only AIA using the SxAIA ISA string alone.

spec_citations.excerpt: Smidctrl depends on the Smcsrind and Smaia extensions. Ssidctrl depends on the Sscsrind and Ssaia extensions.
The AIA eidelivery and eithreshold CSRs defined for the Incoming Message Signaled Interrupt Controller (IMSIC) are not included in the scope of Smidctrl/Ssidctrl.

findings.finding: CPU hotplug online callback calls imsic_state_online() -> imsic_local_delivery(true), which writes IMSIC_EITHRESHOLD and IMSIC_EIDELIVERY. This is the standard IMSIC per-CPU init path and is correct for IMSIC hardware. No SMIDCTRL/SSIDCTRL involvement.
PM resume (CPU_PM_EXIT) re-initializes IMSIC hardware state including eithreshold/eidelivery. Standard IMSIC PM restore path, correct for IMSIC hardware. No ACLIC interaction.

VCPU external interrupt injection checks mrif->eidelivery to decide whether to set IRQ_VS_EXT. This is the IMSIC virtualization path: eidelivery=1 means direct delivery mode in the guest's IMSIC context. Not related to ACLIC Smidctrl/Ssidctrl. The spec confirms that in ACLIC, eip/eie behave as if eidelivery=1 (line 346-347), so this virtualization code would be semantically correct even for ACLIC guests if ACLIC virtualization were added in the future.
